newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent in correction but will then move up.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent in correction but will then move up.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ Brent and gas oil are set to consolidate after the recent sharp upwards movement but the longer term outlook is bullish.
+ June Brent, which expires today, is supported above a gap from $18.94 to $19.00. Resistance is pegged first at $19.89. July Brent closed on Wednesday at $19.54.

IPE Brent crude oil and gas oil futures are expected to sit back at current levels after the recent sharp upwards move but the year's downtrend has now been broken and technical analysts are bullish in the longer term.
June Brent, which expires on Thursday, closed 11 cents a barrel down at $19.51, while July Brent ended eight cents up at $19.54. June gas oil dropped by $2.50 to close at $170.75.

"We see that after the very sharp upwards move we have got into a correction," said Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson Derivatives in the Isle of Man. "That might take another couple of days to work through."
"But the downtrend from the highs in early January was broken a couple of days ago and I expect we are going to go higher."
He said the gap between $18.94 and $19.00 was probably the lowest point likely to be reached in the near term, and added that the initial target was $20.65, the high reached on March 19.
"That is the initial target but because the support at $17.60-$18.00 has been so very well tested, it has made (a base) capable of supporting a move up to $21.50."
Gas oil, he said, was in a similar position.
"Gas oil is equally convincing. The bear trap was set with a test of $160.00 and the market has a really good base."
Initial resistance, he said, would be encountered at Tuesday's high of $174.25 but he said his target lay at $177.25, the high point reached on March 19.
"That should follow in the next week or 10 days but in the longer term I think we are capable of pushing into the broad band of resistance between around $182 and $186."
Mark Schimmel at Elliott Wave International in the U.S. said the July Brent contract would find support first at $19.15.
"Look for a rise above $19.54 to clear the way for new highs in both July and June," he said in a daily report.
June gas oil, he added, would be supported at $170.50 and would find resistance at $173.25 and $174.25.
-- Nicholas Shaxson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8167
